messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] KV cache pressure rising in us-west-2 — continuous-batcher pool7 reporting rapid eviction rate and paging. Severity P1. (auto-detected by perf-alerts)

Maya: saw the alert, paging is spiking and tail latencies climbing to ~2-3s for text-gen endpoints.

Sam: adding context — we pushed a contbatch config change ~10m ago (max_num_seqs: 5000 -> 10000) in canary. timeline lines up.

Jake: yeah that change — can someone roll the canary back? how bad is blast radius?

Eli (support): customer-facing note: 3 customers reported 502/timeouts in last 8m. CS notified Ana.

Ana (customer_success): i'm reaching out to affected customers. need ETA for mitigation to pass along.

Tina (eng-oncall): i'm oncall now. post the exact contbatch config and grafana link pls. i'll take lead on mitigation.

Jake: config snippet:
````
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_num_seqs: 10000
  max_batch_tokens: 65536
  max_batch_size: 2048
  timeout_ms: 30
````
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/contbatch/evictions?orgId=1 (eviction-rate, page-read/s, mem-usage)

Tina: watching metrics — eviction-rate jumped from ~0 to 16k/min in 6m for pool7. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~70%. paging IOPS spiked.

Maya: probable mechanism: TTL-based eviction + sudden huge max_num_seqs expanded working set -> mass eviction and immediate paging for hot prefixes.

Sam: also saw kvstore compaction kicked ~5m ago on the same nodes. two simultaneous stresses likely compound.

OpsLead: mitigation options listed: 1) revert max_num_seqs to 5000 2) disable contbatch on pool7 temporarily 3) force-evict small keys to reclaim memory (risky)

Tina: revert config is lowest risk. Jake, can you push rollback to canary and affected prod pools?

Jake: applying rollback now to pool7 canary and shard in prod. kubectl apply -f contbatch-config-rollback.yaml 
# contbatch.max_num_seqs: 5000
Applied to canary at 3898765560.

Tina: monitoring. @eng-sre stand by for paging/eviction followup.

Ben (eng-sre): standing by. watching swap activity, free page reads and network egress for the cluster.

metrics-bot: Alert: eviction-rate cleared for pool7 at 3898765620 (eviction-rate dropping, paging IOPS down ~65%).

Maya: observed latency trending down to ~250-400ms for affected endpoints. expect customer-visible recovery within 5-10m.

Eli (support): customer update sent: "We've applied a rollback to batching config which is reducing latency. We'll follow up once stability is confirmed." Ana sent updates to customers.

Tina: incident status: mitigation applied and stabilizing. need RCA: why did we push 10k without workload gating? Was canary perf testing sufficient?

Sam: preliminary hypothesis: change lacked workload-specific gating and canary traffic didn't exercise tail-heavy working sets; compaction timing made it worse.

Jake: long-term mitigations proposed: add cache-working-set simulation for config changes; per-pool soft upper bounds (eg 6000 for small-gpu pools); improve canary traffic to include heavy-tail scenarios.

OpsLead: propose an emergency circuit: if eviction-rate > threshold && page-reads > threshold -> autoscale-back max_num_seqs or flip contbatch to degrade-safe mode.

Tina: agree. i'll keep the incident ticket open and schedule a postmortem. tagging @Sam @Jake @Maya @Eli for followups.

Ana: customers confirmed recovery. one asked for a short timeline and RCA note — i'll need that for the follow-up.

Tina: timeline to capture for the postmortem: 3898765432 (alert), 3898765440 (config rollout), 3898765560 (rollback applied to canary), 3898765620 (metrics stabilized). i'll draft the incident doc and share.

Maya: adding action items to backlog: contbatch config vetting, guardrails, improved alerts for cache pressure, and canary traffic enhancements.

Tina: closing active mitigation loop. leaving thread open for post-incident items. great coordination, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> downgraded to P2 (stability restored). Postmortem requested.
